svg.text: Teryx OS wiring, sheet 'trailer'. Made from config/wiring.yaml by `python -m teryx wiring`. Don't edit this file.
Labels: wire id, size, fuse (if the wire has its own), and anything in between. Faded = optional. Hover for notes. Full table: docs/wiring/README.md

g.title: T05: BRAKE_SW.OUT -> TRAILER.P6_STOP - Trailer brake lights still work with the control box off
T06: RELAYS.NO1 -> TRAILER.P2_REV - Reversing pin. Relay 1 also runs the floods by hand, so trailer reverse lights would come on with them
T07: RELAYS.NO7 -> TCAM_PLUG.V12 - 2 A inline fuse. Runs while driving, not just reversing
T11: TCAM_PLUG.VID -> TCAM_DONGLE.VID - Shielded video cable
T13: FB.IN -> TCAM_PLUG.LB_POS - Own 10 A inline fuse off the fuse block's feed stud (the 12-way is full)
TRAILER: 7-pin flat trailer socket (Narva 82043BL, reed switch)

RELAYS: 16-ch relay board, channels 1-8 - One 16-channel board of mechanical 5 V relays with opto and JD-VCC jumper (AliExpress cart), in an aux box next to the control box. RELAYS2 is channels 9-16 of the same board. The solid state G3MB-202P board Sam has is AC only and won't turn off on 12 V DC. JD-VCC jumper off, coils on 5 V, inputs from 3.3 V

FB: Blade fuse block - 12 fuses in use. Small loads that can go out together share a fuse (front bars in pairs, trailer tail + stop, interior bar + accessory). All four front bars are NOT on one fuse, so one fault can't black out the front at night. The winch, control box power, key, power hold and each actuator keep their own. Sam's 12-way (in the post) is used, so it is full with no spares; add a small 6-way next to it if more circuits come

TCAM_PLUG: Trailer EU 7-pin round plug (camera + light bar, Sam's) - Sam's EU round 7-pin, next to the flat NZ/AU 7-pin for the main trailer lights, so they can't be mixed up. NOT wired to the EU light standard. 1 cam +12 V, 2 video, 3 cam ground, 4 video shield, 5 light bar +12 V, 6 light bar - (switched), 7 spare. Light bar on 1.5 mm² (pins are good for 10 A+). Spring cap on the socket and dielectric grease on the pins

TCAM_DONGLE: Analogue video to camera-ribbon (CSI) board, ADV7280-M (rear + trailer) - No USB (Sam). The cameras run in CVBS (PAL) mode into this board, which sits in the Pi box on the Pi's 2nd camera ribbon port. ADV7280-M has several analogue inputs picked in software (adv728x-m overlay, adv7180 driver), so it swaps rear/trailer itself, no relay. A spare input can take a small cabin camera later. Pi 5 support for these boards is not proven yet: bench test it first
LB_TRL: Trailer light bar (Sam's spare) - On the trailer, through the 8-pin plug. On/off from the dash and the phone remote; only live when the trailer plug is in

MOSFET: 8-ch isolated MOSFET board (low side, 6 used, 2 spare) - One 8-channel opto-isolated MOSFET board (3.3 V input version), one channel per light bar, 3 spare. About 6 A per front bar. Low side switching, so each bar's + comes from its fuse and its - goes to an OUT pin

PCA: PCA9685 16-ch PWM board (0x40) - More dimming outputs on the Pico's I2C. Wires soldered straight to the pads, no header pins. VCC 3.3 V so the outputs are 3.3 V, which the 3.3 V PNP MOSFET board takes. Leave V+ (servo power) empty. OE tied low on the board. 15 channels spare
